home-remodeling.title: Hollywood Lakes, FL Home Remodeling | PGX Builders
home-remodeling.meta_description: 1920s Mediterranean and mid-century houses east of Young Circle in Hollywood Lakes, rebuilt behind the original walls. (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.h1: Old house, new everything behind it
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Full-gut remodels for the 1920s Mediterraneans and postwar houses around North and South Lake, permitted through the City of Hollywood Building Division, supervised daily, and built by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Hollywood Lakes is the part of Joseph Wesley Young's 1920s plan you can still read on the ground: two dredged lakes flanking Hollywood Boulevard, president-named streets running east to the Intracoastal, and Mediterranean Revival houses with barrel tile and arched porches sitting a block from postwar ranches. Owners along North Lake Drive, Harrison Street and Madison Street rarely knock these down. They gut them instead, opening compartmented front rooms, replacing every mechanical system in the building, and swapping jalousies for impact glass, all without changing what the street looks like from the sidewalk.

The permit comes from the City of Hollywood's Building Division inside Development Services, not from the county. Behind that sits the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which hears appeals of building and fire code officials' decisions, issues formal interpretations of disputed code sections, and backs Broward's own administrative chapter of the Florida Building Code. Most of the neighborhood sits inside the Lakes Area Historic Multiple Resource Listing District or the Hollywood Lakes Historic District, so exterior work on a covered property needs a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic Preservation Board. Broward sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so windows, doors and roofing need HVHZ approvals.

This is our twentieth-plus year building in South Florida, with over 150 remodels and additions delivered and every one permitted and inspected. On these blocks that means a fixed written scope signed before the first wall comes down, a supervisor on site each working day, original terrazzo and millwork protected before demolition rather than apologized for afterward, and a job site that leaves a narrow lakefront street passable for your neighbors. One licensed team carries the work from estimate through final inspection and warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets demolished before the scope is written down. Here is the work a Hollywood Lakes whole-house project usually covers, roughly in the order it happens.

scope_items.name: Opening the 1920s plan
scope_items.desc: Taking out partitions between front rooms, dining rooms and the old kitchen wing, with sealed calculations and steel or engineered beams where original framing needs help.

scope_items.name: New service, new mechanicals
scope_items.desc: Upgraded electrical service and panels, replacement supply and drain lines, and right-sized duct and equipment instead of systems designed around window units.

scope_items.name: Impact glass in arched openings
scope_items.desc: Windows and doors carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approvals, chosen in profiles that suit an arched Mediterranean opening rather than flattening it.

scope_items.name: Roof, tie-beam and truss repair
scope_items.desc: The structural work found once ceilings open: tired tie-beams, rotted framing and decking brought up to current attachment requirements while access is still free.

scope_items.name: Finishes in the right order
scope_items.desc: Millwork, stone, tile and paint sequenced so trades are not working on top of each other, and so the punch list is short rather than legendary.

faqs.q: Is my Hollywood Lakes house in a historic district?
faqs.a: Quite possibly. The city runs two overlapping designations here, the Lakes Area Historic Multiple Resource Listing District and the Hollywood Lakes Historic District, and the Historic Preservation Board issues Certificates of Appropriateness for Design and for Demolition on properties inside them. Purely interior work usually moves without a board hearing. Anything that changes a designated exterior needs its certificate before the building permit advances, so we confirm your property's status with the Division of Planning and Urban Design before drawings start.

faqs.q: Who issues the permit, the city or Broward County?
faqs.a: The city. Your permit and inspections go through the Building Division inside Hollywood's Development Services Department. Broward County's Board of Rules and Appeals sits behind that process countywide: it considers code amendments, hears appeals of building and fire code officials, and renders formal interpretations when a code section is disputed. Broward also maintains its own administrative chapter of the Florida Building Code. You deal with the city; we deal with both.

faqs.q: We are two blocks from the Intracoastal. Does the flood zone change our remodel?
faqs.a: It can. Properties in a mapped flood zone fall under federal substantial improvement rules, which compare what you are investing against the value of the existing structure. Cross that threshold and the whole building has to be brought into flood compliance, which is a very different project than a gut renovation. The city's floodplain staff will confirm your zone. We run that math before design, not during permitting.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-house remodel take in the Lakes?
faqs.a: Plan on two phases. Design, engineering, any historic review and plan check commonly occupy several months before a permit issues, and construction on a full house typically runs from several months to about a year depending on structure, mechanical scope and how much of the exterior changes. Custom millwork and long-lead openings drive the tail end. The schedule arrives with the estimate, and a supervisor is accountable for holding it.

faqs.q: What does a gut renovation of a Lakes house cost?
faqs.a: Honestly, it depends on how much of the building stays. Re-plumbing, re-wiring, new air handling and HVHZ openings on a 1920s masonry house cost real money before anyone picks a tile. We would rather scope it precisely than float a number that grows by change order, so you get a fixed written scope with named allowances. PGX is a high-end contractor and rarely the lowest of three bids; clients hire us for the certainty.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Come with the old plans, the wish list, or nothing but frustration. What comes back is a priced scope and an honest schedule, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchens Rebuilt in Hollywood Lakes, FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Kitchen remodeling for Hollywood Lakes homes: cabinetry scribed to 1920s walls, islands set on sound floors, permits handled. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: A kitchen the whole house uses
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and genuine layout changes for Hollywood Lakes kitchens, with appliance relocations, new circuits and gas runs permitted through the City of Hollywood and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Where the kitchen wants to be now
intro_paragraphs: Walk into almost any original house between Young Circle and the Intracoastal and the kitchen is in the wrong place. Boom-era builders tucked it at the back corner, walled off from the dining room, sized for a cook nobody employs anymore. The 1950s and 1960s houses on Jefferson Street and Van Buren Street are only slightly kinder. So kitchen remodeling in Hollywood Lakes usually means absorbing a pantry or breakfast nook, taking down one masonry wall, and giving the room a real island with sightlines to the yard or the lake.

A kitchen that stays inside the walls is permitted through Hollywood's Building Division with plumbing, electrical, mechanical and gas inspections along the way, and no Historic Preservation Board hearing. Change something visible from the street or the water on a designated property, such as enlarging the window over the sink or venting a hood through a front facade, and a Certificate of Appropriateness comes first. Add the practical Broward realities: HVHZ approvals for any new opening, and older services that will not carry an induction range, a wine cooler and two ovens without an upgrade.

Cabinetry is unforgiving, so we treat it that way. Boxes are ordered against field measurements taken after demolition, stone is templated once the cabinets are set rather than off a drawing, and the plumbing rough-in is located to the fixture you actually bought. You get a fixed written scope, daily supervision, dust barriers that respect the rest of a finished house, and one accountable team. More than 150 remodels and additions delivered across South Florida, all permitted and inspected, licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072.

scope_items.desc: Stone islands with the substructure engineered for weight, seating overhangs properly supported, and levelness checked against terrazzo that predates everyone in the room.

scope_items.desc: Structural openings between kitchen, dining and family space, with engineered headers, sealed drawings and the permit that keeps it legal at resale.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to redo a kitchen in Hollywood?
faqs.a: For anything past paint and appliance swaps, yes. Moving plumbing, altering circuits, adding gas or changing structure all pull permits through the City of Hollywood Building Division, with inspections before things are closed up. That sequence is worth having: it means the rough-in was verified before the tile went on. Unpermitted kitchens surface during title and inspection when the house sells, and fixing them retroactively costs more than doing it once.

faqs.q: Will the Historic Preservation Board get involved in my kitchen?
faqs.a: Only if your scope reaches the outside of a designated property. The board's review covers historic sites and properties inside the city's historic districts, through Certificates of Appropriateness for Design and for Demolition. An interior kitchen stays with plan review. Enlarging the sink window, cutting a new door to the terrace or punching a hood vent through a visible wall changes that, and a Certificate of Appropriateness comes before the building permit. We identify which path applies at the first walk-through.

faqs.q: The house is on a slab. Can the sink and island move anywhere?
faqs.a: Mostly, with two constraints worth naming early. Drain lines need fall, so moving a sink far from the existing stack sometimes means cutting and re-routing under slab or accepting a different island location. Older cast iron found during that cut is usually worth replacing while it is exposed. We open a small investigative area before finalizing the layout so the plan you approve is the plan we can actually build.

faqs.q: How far ahead do we need to order cabinets?
faqs.a: Further than most people expect. Custom cabinet packages are measured, drawn, approved and then fabricated, and that runway is usually the longest single item on the schedule. We order early and hold demolition until the delivery window is real, so your house is not living without a kitchen while a shop finishes doors. Appliances with long lead times get selected in the same conversation for exactly the same reason.

faqs.q: Where does a Lakes kitchen budget go?
faqs.a: Cabinetry, stone and appliances set the number, and behind-the-wall work moves it more than clients expect on an older house. Rather than quote a range that means nothing, we walk the space, confirm what the structure and services need, and put a fixed written figure against a written specification. If the deciding factor is the cheapest bid, we will say so early and part on friendly terms.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Rebuilding Bathrooms in Hollywood Lakes, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Rebuilding baths in Hollywood Lakes, FL, where 1920s plumbing hides behind new marble. Permitted, inspected, supervised daily. (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs for Hollywood Lakes homes, with flood-tested pans, verified slope and every plumbing and electrical permit pulled through the City of Hollywood, supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: What is behind a Lakes bathroom wall
intro_paragraphs: A 1926 house on Monroe Street was built with one bathroom and a hall. The ranches that filled in during the 1950s added a second, then tiled it in a color that has since become a conversation piece. Neither arrangement resembles what buyers and long-term owners in Hollywood Lakes want now: a primary suite with two vanities, a freestanding tub, and a shower that does not require choreography. Most bathroom remodeling here is really space planning, borrowing a closet, a hall or a small back bedroom to make one good room.

Plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits come from the City of Hollywood Building Division, with inspections before anything gets covered. Interior bath work almost never sees the Historic Preservation Board; adding or enlarging a window on a designated facade does, through a Certificate of Appropriateness. Any new opening also needs High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approval, since all of Broward is HVHZ. If you own in one of the older low-rise buildings near the water, add association approval and the scheduling reality of Florida's milestone inspection and structural reserve requirements to the front end.

Bathrooms fail quietly and expensively, so we build them like small pieces of infrastructure. Waterproofing membranes are flood-tested before tile, slopes are confirmed with a level instead of an opinion, heavy glass hangs on blocking installed for that purpose, and stone is set by people who have earned the right to handle it. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, protected pathways from the front door to the work zone, and a licensed, insured contractor behind all of it. Lic. CGC1539072, permitted and inspected without exception.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: How a bath project is built
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: From a powder room to a full primary suite, the specification is settled in writing before tile is ordered. These are the elements that carry the job.

scope_items.name: Making a real primary suite
scope_items.desc: Borrowing a closet, hall or back bedroom and reworking walls and rough-ins so the suite reads as original rather than assembled from leftovers.

scope_items.name: The membrane under the marble
scope_items.desc: Membranes filled and held before a single tile goes down, linear or center drains set to measured slope, and curbless entries where the slab allows.

scope_items.name: Tubs the structure supports
scope_items.desc: Freestanding tub placement checked against floor framing, filler routing planned in advance, and stone surfaces sealed for daily use in Florida humidity.

scope_items.name: Replacing the original plumbing

scope_items.name: Glass, light and quiet air

faqs.q: Does a bathroom remodel in Hollywood need a permit?
faqs.a: Anything beyond a cosmetic refresh does. Relocating or replacing plumbing, altering circuits, adding a heated floor or changing ventilation all require permits and inspections through the City of Hollywood Building Division. The value is not paperwork for its own sake; it is a third party confirming the rough plumbing and waterproofing before marble hides them forever. We pull the permits, book the inspections and hand you the closed-out record at the end.

faqs.q: Our house is a designated historic property. Can we still redo the bathrooms?
faqs.a: Yes. The Historic Preservation Board's concern is the exterior and the character of designated buildings, and it acts on Certificates of Appropriateness for Design and Demolition inside Hollywood's historic districts. Interior bathrooms are generally yours to redesign. A new or enlarged window, a relocated exterior vent or a change to the facade brings a Certificate of Appropriateness into the sequence. That adds calendar time, not a veto, and we build it into the schedule from the start.

faqs.q: Can we move a bathroom to the other side of the house?
faqs.a: Often, though the slab decides how graceful it is. Drains need fall and vents need a path, so a bath far from the existing stack can mean saw-cutting slab, re-routing under it, or running a new vent up through a wall cavity that may not exist yet. On second floors the framing sets the limits. We investigate before design so you are choosing between real options rather than discovering constraints mid-demolition.

faqs.q: We own in an older low-rise near the Intracoastal. What is different?
faqs.a: Timing, mostly. Expect an association architectural approval, proof of insurance for the contractor, restrictions on work hours and elevator use, and coordination for building water shutoffs that affect neighbors. Older buildings of three stories or more also sit inside Florida's milestone inspection and structural reserve study framework, which can put building-wide work on the calendar alongside yours. We schedule around the building's rules rather than arguing with them.

faqs.q: What does a primary bath at this level run?
faqs.a: Stone, glass and fixtures are visible costs; drains, supply, venting and waterproofing are the ones people underestimate, and in a house from the 1920s or 1950s they are usually the bigger half. We scope what the building genuinely needs and give you a fixed written number rather than a per-square-foot guess. As a high-end contractor we compete on finish quality and certainty, not on being cheapest.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Tell us what is wrong with it and we will come measure, scope it in writing, and price it honestly, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions in Hollywood Lakes, FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Additions for Hollywood Lakes homes, engineered and reviewed for the historic district: rear wings, second stories, family suites. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, garage conversions and in-law suites for Hollywood Lakes homes, with foundations and tie-beams engineered, historic review handled where required, permits through the City of Hollywood and daily site supervision.
home-additions.local_heading: Adding on inside a historic district
intro_paragraphs: Hollywood Lakes was platted on fifty-foot lots with garages at the back and service alleys running behind every street. A 1920s two-bedroom on Tyler Street or a compact ranch on Jackson Street usually has room behind it and a way to get materials there without parading them past the front door, which is why so many owners here extend rather than list. The common projects are a rear family room and primary suite pushed into the back yard, a second story added over an original single-story plan, a garage turned into conditioned space, and an in-law suite for a household that has grown in both directions.

Hollywood's Building Division looks hard at exactly this kind of work. Zoning setbacks, lot coverage and height are reviewed by the Division of Planning and Urban Design, the Building Division permits the construction, and on a designated property inside a historic district the Historic Preservation Board weighs massing and materials through a Certificate of Appropriateness. Expect sealed structural engineering for footings, tie-beams and uplift, HVHZ product approvals for every new opening, and for lots near the Intracoastal, a hard look at flood zone and federal substantial improvement limits before anyone draws a wall.

Additions are where two decades of South Florida work actually shows. Tying a new footing to a 1920s foundation, matching stucco texture and barrel tile so the seam disappears, and keeping the occupied half of the house livable while the other half has no roof are all learned skills. PGX runs the project on a fixed written scope with a supervisor on site daily, coordinates the engineer and the reviews, and keeps one accountable team from the first feasibility conversation through final inspection and warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Each of these starts with engineering and an honest read of the review it will face. We would rather kill a bad idea in week one than at plan check.

scope_items.desc: Family rooms, primary suites and enlarged dining space pushed into the yard, with foundation, tie-beam and roof tie-in designed and permitted as one package.

scope_items.name: Second stories over old walls
scope_items.desc: Existing masonry and footings evaluated by an engineer first, then an upper floor designed to satisfy both the structure and the district's massing expectations.

scope_items.name: Garage and carport conversions
scope_items.desc: Turning unconditioned space into legal living area, insulated and conditioned, with openings and mechanical work permitted so it counts when you sell.

scope_items.name: A private family wing
scope_items.desc: Independent suites with bath, closet and kitchenette for long-stay family, scaled to the original architecture instead of appearing to have landed there.

scope_items.name: Footings, tie-beams and uplift
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, steel and continuous load path work: the invisible half of the budget, and the half that decides whether the addition lasts.

faqs.q: Does an addition in Hollywood Lakes need Historic Preservation Board approval?
faqs.a: If your property is designated or sits inside one of Hollywood's historic districts, plan on it. The board's duties cover projects on historic sites and inside historic districts, and additions to existing single-family houses come to it as Certificates of Appropriateness for Design. That certificate comes before the building permit advances. Designs that respect the original roof line, proportions and materials tend to move cleanly; designs that fight the house invite revisions and a second hearing.

faqs.q: Can a 1920s masonry house carry a second story?
faqs.a: Many can, some need reinforcement, and a structural engineer settles it rather than a contractor's instinct. Original clay tile, oolitic limestone or concrete block walls and shallow footings are evaluated first, then new columns, thickened footings or upgraded tie-beams are designed where the numbers require them. Occasionally the honest answer is that a rear extension gives you more usable space for less money. We put both options in front of you with real figures attached.

faqs.q: How does the flood zone affect an addition near the water?
faqs.a: It can reshape the whole project. In a mapped flood zone, federal substantial improvement rules measure your investment against the value of the existing structure, and crossing that threshold obligates you to bring the entire building into flood compliance rather than just the new part. On lots close to the Intracoastal that changes the design conversation entirely. Hollywood's floodplain staff confirm your zone, and we run the analysis before you commit to drawings.

faqs.q: How long does an addition take start to finish?
faqs.a: Front-load your expectations. Design, structural engineering, historic review where it applies, zoning confirmation and plan check commonly take several months before ground is broken, and construction on a substantial addition runs several months more, longer if a second story is involved. About a year from first meeting to move-in is a realistic frame for a serious project. The full timeline goes in writing so no phase arrives as a surprise.

faqs.q: What does an addition cost per square foot here?
faqs.a: Per-square-foot numbers mislead on additions, because foundations, structure, roof tie-ins and mechanical extensions do not scale with floor area. A simple rear extension and a second story over an unreinforced house are entirely different budgets. After a site visit and a structural read we give you a fixed written scope. We build at a high-end level and price accordingly, with the number tied to a specification rather than a hope.

home-additions.cta_sub: Show us the lot, the survey and what you are missing. You get a candid feasibility read and honest numbers, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.local_heading: Shade, salt air and the Intracoastal
intro_paragraphs: Young laid this neighborhood out around water and shade, and a century later that is still the point. Houses on North Lake Drive and South Lake Drive look across open water; the streets east toward the Intracoastal end at seawalls and dockage with a run north to the Port Everglades inlet. Under mature banyans and royal palms, owners are building the outdoor half of the house: a covered terrace off the rear, a summer kitchen that works in August, a pergola over the pool deck, and a driveway and entry that finally match the front elevation.

Exterior work triggers the most review in Hollywood Lakes. Structures need building permits from the City of Hollywood Building Division, gas, water and electrical runs need their own trade permits, and on a designated property in a historic district the Historic Preservation Board reviews visible changes through a Certificate of Appropriateness. Seawall and dock work runs through the city plus Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program, which licenses work in, on or under surface waters, including docks, seawalls, dredge and fill and mangrove trimming. Hollywood has also adopted minimum seawall and tidal barrier elevations in step with Broward County's countywide standard.

Exterior work gets interior standards here, because the weather does not grade on a curve. Pergola footings are engineered rather than estimated, terraces are pitched to move water away from the house instead of toward the slab, and anything within reach of salt air gets marine-grade metal, sealed dense stone and hardware chosen for the exposure. Projects run on a fixed written scope with daily supervision and a site that gets cleaned every afternoon. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072, with more than 20 years of South Florida construction behind the estimate.

scope_items.desc: Patching spalled stucco, repairing coastal corrosion at lintels and rails, and repainting properly, which on a designated facade means color approval first.

scope_items.name: Impact openings and re-roof
scope_items.desc: HVHZ-approved terrace doors and exterior units installed with flashing done right, and roofing sequenced with the rest so the work happens once.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for a pergola or a summer kitchen in Hollywood?
faqs.a: Yes, on both counts, and usually more than one. The structure itself needs a building permit from the City of Hollywood, and the gas, water and electrical runs each carry their own trade permit and inspection. If the property is designated or the work is visible within a historic district, add Historic Preservation Board review before the permit moves. It is more process than a grill island appears to deserve, and it is what keeps the work insurable and legal.

faqs.q: We need the seawall and dock rebuilt. Who approves that?
faqs.a: More than one agency. The city permits the construction, and Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program licenses work in, on or under surface waters, which covers docks, seawalls, dredge and fill and mangrove trimming. State and federal review can apply depending on the scope. Hollywood also sets minimum seawall and tidal barrier elevations built around projected sea level rise, in step with the county's countywide standard. Expect a real approval runway, and plan around it.

faqs.q: Can the pool deck and the re-roof happen at the same time?
faqs.a: They usually should. Roof edges, gutters, downspouts and terrace drainage are one system, and re-roofing after a new terrace is finished means dropping tile and equipment onto fresh work. We sequence roofing, exterior openings and hardscape in a single schedule under one contractor, so flashing details tie into the new structure and you are not living through two separate construction seasons for related work.

faqs.q: Does the Historic Preservation Board review a driveway or a fence?
faqs.a: It can, when the property is designated or the change reads from the street inside a historic district. The board's review covers substantial alterations to designated buildings and sites, and front-yard hardscape, fencing, exterior color and anything altering the presentation of a historic facade fall within that conversation. It has issued a Certificate of Appropriateness for something as ordinary as a circular driveway. Rear-yard work screened from view is usually simpler. We confirm the property's designation status with the Division of Planning and Urban Design before design begins.

faqs.q: What drives the cost of an outdoor room here?
faqs.a: It scales with structure and utilities more than with area. A paver terrace and drainage is one budget; a covered outdoor room with a summer kitchen, gas, water, electrical and engineered footings is genuinely another, and appliance and stone selections move it further. After a site walk you get a written scope with real specifications, so you are comparing what is actually being built rather than a per-foot figure that ignores what sits under the slab.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: A city desk with a historic layer
intro_paragraphs: Hollywood Lakes hands its permit trouble down with the deed. A 1920s Mediterranean on Harrison Street changes hands three times, and somewhere in that chain a garage became a bedroom, jalousies became impact windows, and a Florida room appeared off the back with nothing in the city file to show for it. Nobody notices until a title search, an appraiser or a lender does, usually with a closing date already on the calendar. On the lots running east toward the Intracoastal, add a dock or a seawall repair built and never inspected. None of it is a construction problem. All of it is a records problem.

Permits come from the Building Division inside Hollywood's Development Services Department. Applications, uploads and inspection requests now run through the city's Accela Citizen Access portal, while anything pulled before that changeover still lives in the older system, where most inherited files turn up. Behind the city sits a countywide code layer: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the county amendments to the Florida Building Code and certifies the plans examiners and inspectors who read your file. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so openings and roofing need approved products. On a designated property, a Certificate of Appropriateness comes first.

Twenty-plus years in South Florida and more than 150 permitted, inspected remodels and additions mostly teach you to read a bad file quickly. We start with the record and a walk-through, open whatever has to be opened, and retain the engineer, architect or surveyor the city will want to see rather than claiming those licenses ourselves. Close to the Intracoastal we check the flood side early, since federal substantial improvement limits can reshape a scope before it is priced. The scope is fixed and written, a supervisor is on site daily, and whoever ran the work meets the inspector. Nobody here will offer you a shortcut.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: First the file, then the work
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Some of this starts as a plan for new work. The rest starts as something a previous owner left behind. Both begin the same way, with the record read end to end.

scope_items.name: Permits inherited with the deed
scope_items.desc: Pulling the full permit history for the address, matching it against what is physically standing, then reviving, amending or re-inspecting each one until the city calls it closed.

scope_items.name: Unpermitted work, legalized
scope_items.desc: Conversions and extensions that never reached a plan sheet, surveyed and drawn as they actually exist, reinforced where an engineer says so, then inspected into the record.

scope_items.name: Impact glass with approvals
scope_items.desc: Openings and roofing tied to approvals valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, with anchoring submitted and installed exactly as the approval reads rather than by habit.

scope_items.name: Inspections, called and met
scope_items.desc: Trade and structural inspections sequenced so nothing gets covered too early, each met on site by the supervisor who ran the work, through to the last signature.

scope_items.name: Recertification repairs, permitted
scope_items.desc: Concrete restoration, railings, waterproofing and electrical work that a safety inspection or milestone report puts on a building's list, priced, permitted and built as one package.

faqs.q: There is an open permit on our Hollywood Lakes house and the closing is set. What now?
faqs.a: Order the record first. The city can show every permit issued at the address, which inspections were signed and where the file stalled, and permits predating the Accela changeover are searched in the older system. Then comes the diagnosis. Sometimes only the final was never called. Sometimes what stands no longer matches what was approved. Sometimes the permit sits under a contractor who is long gone. All three have a path and none of them is quick, which is the argument for calling now rather than the week of funding.

faqs.q: What actually needs a permit on a house like ours?
faqs.a: More than owners expect. Structure, roofing, windows and doors, electrical, plumbing, gas and mechanical work all do, and so do fences, driveways, pools, docks and seawall repair, which on the Intracoastal side also involves Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program. Paint, flooring over a sound slab and a like-for-like cabinet swap generally do not. What quietly goes unfiled is the expensive kind later: an enclosed porch, a panel upgrade, a water heater moved across the room.

faqs.q: The windows were replaced without a permit and the house is in a historic district. How bad is that?
faqs.a: Fixable, but it is two problems rather than one. The building side needs the units documented against High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals and inspected, which sometimes means proving anchoring nobody photographed at the time. The preservation side runs separately: on a designated property the Historic Preservation Board acts on Certificates of Appropriateness for exterior change, so profiles and materials that were never reviewed get looked at now. We confirm your designation status with the Division of Planning and Urban Design before proposing anything.

faqs.q: Does building recertification or a milestone inspection reach a house here?
faqs.a: Rarely a house. Broward runs a building safety inspection program under the county Board of Rules and Appeals, enforced locally by the City of Hollywood, and it is aimed at older multi-family and commercial buildings, with a floor-area threshold worth checking on a very large house. Florida's milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more, which here means the older low-rise buildings at the edges. The report belongs to a licensed engineer or architect; the repairs are ours.

faqs.q: What does it cost to clear all of this up?
faqs.a: It depends on what the record is hiding. Work that is sound and simply never had its final called is a modest line item. Framing put up without engineering, or a roof laid without approved products, can mean opening it back up and rebuilding to current code, which is a real number. Fees are set by the city and rise with the value of the work, so nobody can quote them off an address. You get a written scope with the bad news already in it.

permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the number, the title report or just the address, and you get a written read on what it takes to clear the file, in English o en español.
